fields.why: The number of naloxone doses per patient is a count; the brief says a count outcome analyzed with a linear method (here a t-test of means) stays count/rate, with the procedure recording the t-test.

All claims are 8-mg vs 4-mg contrasts; B's summary rests on a per-group mean that is one side of that contrast, though the overall 75.6% hospital transport figure would support summary as a minor single quantity.

The report form collects 'age and perceived gender of the aided person', so sex is as present as age (descriptor, level 0); A's age entry cites only the 'demographics' limitation, which names neither.

brief_issues: Both readers found that the table's 'RR' values reproduce odds ratios, contradicting the stated log-binomial model; the brief does not say whether the family should follow the stated model (loglinear) or the reported estimates (logistic). Both used loglinear, B with a logistic alternative_reading, which seems the right handling.
